description: A freelance designer must decide whether to accept a photographer's offer to trade a promotional poster for a family photo session, while an event organizer and a former client help settle the exact deliverables and rights.

shared_context.S1: Cal has offered Rina a family photo session in exchange for a promotional poster for his weekend pop-up photo booth.
shared_context.S2: Rina decides whether to proceed and sets the final terms of the service swap.
shared_context.S3: The poster will be used to promote Cal's photo booth at an upcoming neighborhood event.
shared_context.S4: Rina's normal swap routine is to take one concise practical-terms report from Cal, then Mei, then Jonah, in that order, before she makes the final call. Each person gives their report on their first turn, and Rina may ask one follow-up before settling.

PF1.text: Cal is available to conduct the family photo session only on Saturday, June 15, and he can deliver exactly 40 edited digital photos by June 20.

PF2.text: Mei confirmed with the event printer that the poster must be an 18-by-24-inch PDF at 300 dpi, and the printer needs 100 copies.

PF3.text: Jonah previously hired Cal and learned that Cal's usual package grants only personal-use rights; promotional use requires an explicit perpetual license, which Jonah did not receive on his own booking.

acceptance_conditions: The swap must proceed as a poster-design-for-family-photo-session exchange.
The photo session must be scheduled for Saturday, June 15.
The settlement must provide exactly 40 edited digital photos by June 20.
The poster must be specified as 18 inches by 24 inches in PDF format at 300 dpi.
The settlement must include exactly 100 printed copies of the poster.
Cal must grant Rina an explicit perpetual promotional-use license for the photos.
The promotional-use license must be logged as a commitment and PF3 must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C4: decisions['poster_width_inches'] == 18 and decisions['poster_height_inches'] == 24 and decisions['poster_file_type'] == 'PDF' and decisions['poster_resolution_dpi'] == 300
content_checks.C7: any((c['type'] == 'promotional_license' and c['target'] == 'Rina') or (c['type'] == 'licensing' and c['target'] == 'Cal') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Cal's private availability fixes the session date at Saturday, June 15, while his stated capacity fixes the deliverable at exactly 40 edited photos by June 20.
The printer's requirements change the poster into an 18-by-24-inch PDF at exactly 300 dpi with exactly 100 printed copies.
Jonah's prior booking shows that personal-use rights are insufficient, changing the license field to the exact term perpetual and requiring a logged promotional-license commitment justified by PF3.
